/** How a run's pull request stands, as the git host last said. */
export type PrState = NonNullable<AgentMeta['prState']>

/**
 * A run's pull request, one glyph per state in the git host's own colours, wherever the run's
 * request is marked (its row in the sidebar, the row under its message box), so a list of runs
 * says which have work waiting for review and which landed without opening one. Each state has its
 * own shape too, for a reader who cannot tell the colours apart. A request whose state is not
 * known, older than the git host lists or not read yet, has no mark: a plain one read as one more
 * state. Its number is still said.
 */
export const PR_MARKS: Record<PrState, { Icon: ComponentType<{ className?: string; 'aria-hidden'?: boolean }>; tone: string; word: string }> = {
  open: { Icon: GitPullRequest, tone: 'text-success', word: 'open' },
  draft: { Icon: GitPullRequestDraft, tone: 'text-muted-foreground', word: 'draft' },
  merged: { Icon: GitMerge, tone: 'text-merged', word: 'merged' },
  closed: { Icon: GitPullRequestClosed, tone: 'text-danger', word: 'closed' },
}

/** A request's state as the git host spells it (`OPEN`, `MERGED`, `CLOSED`) or as a mark names it (`draft`), as a mark's; none for one not known. */
export function prStateOf(hostState: string): PrState | undefined {
  const state = hostState.toLowerCase()
  return state === 'open' || state === 'draft' || state === 'merged' || state === 'closed' ? state : undefined
}

I fixed it so the sidebar row, the session header and the bar under the box now show a PR's new state at the same time, and opened PR #2400: https://github.com/openagt/openagent/pull/2400

**Why the row was behind:** the row and the session page get a PR's state from two different lookups. The sidebar row uses one lookup of all the project's PRs. The header and the bar use a lookup of just the session's branch. Each result was kept for a minute and refreshed on its own schedule. The sidebar list also only reloads every 15 seconds. So once the session page had seen "merged", the row could keep the old "open" answer for a minute or more.

**The fix** (mainly in `packages/ui/src/dashboard/pull-requests.ts`):
- **One answer per PR:** whenever any lookup returns a PR, its state is saved as the latest for that PR. The sidebar row, the header, the bar and the Human Queue's list of open PRs all show that latest state. An older lookup that finishes late doesn't overwrite a newer answer.
- **Reload together:** when a lookup finds that a PR's state changed, the server tells the page through the existing change stream. The sidebar list and the session's own PR information then reload at once, instead of waiting for their next timed refresh.

**Tests:**
- **The new test:** the branch lookup sees the PR merged while the project-wide answer still says open. Without the fix it fails with `'open' !== 'merged'`; with it, it passes.
- **Also added:** tests for the late older lookup, for the server telling the page, and for the page reloading.
- **Checks run:** `pnpm build` and `pnpm typecheck` pass. In the test run for `@openagt/ui` and the two packages that depend on it, everything passed except one test of the demo project. That test reads git's author settings from the environment, and this session sets its own author name and email. I fixed it so the sidebar row, the session header and the bar under the box now show a PR's new state at the same time, and opened PR #2400: https://github.com/openagt/openagent/pull/2400

**Why the row was behind:** the row and the session page get a PR's state from two different lookups. The sidebar row uses one lookup of all the project's PRs. The header and the bar use a lookup of just the session's branch. Each result was kept for a minute and refreshed on its own schedule. The sidebar list also only reloads every 15 seconds. So once the session page had seen "merged", the row could keep the old "open" answer for a minute or more.

**The fix** (mainly in `packages/ui/src/dashboard/pull-requests.ts`):
- **One answer per PR:** whenever any lookup returns a PR, its state is saved as the latest for that PR. The sidebar row, the header, the bar and the Human Queue's list of open PRs all show that latest state. An older lookup that finishes late doesn't overwrite a newer answer.
- **Reload together:** when a lookup finds that a PR's state changed, the server tells the page through the existing change stream. The sidebar list and the session's own PR information then reload at once, instead of waiting for their next timed refresh.
